answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds agent identities to a cryptographic stake burning curve: minting n counterfeit identities requires destroying burned collateral scaled to O(n^2), imposing superlinear economic friction. Malicious entities cannot freely wander across identity pools when each attempt burns verifiable capital. This mathematical barrier acts like a protective orchard, while an incoming tide of dynamic burn fees drains attacker reserves exponentially.
